name: Benchmark
history: Benchmark was founded in Menlo Park in 1995 by Bob Kagle, Bruce Dunlevie, Andy Rachleff, Kevin Harvey and Val Vaden, and built its reputation on an equal partnership with no junior or senior partners, no CEO and no name on the door. Bob Kagle's $6.7 million Series A into eBay in 1997 for about 22% became the best-performing venture investment in Silicon Valley history, and the same first-institutional-round pattern produced Juniper Networks, Red Hat, Equinix and Handspring before 2000, then Yelp, Zillow, OpenTable, Zuora, New Relic and Asana, then Bill Gurley's $11 million Series A into Uber in 2011, Matt Cohler's $7 million into Instagram the same year, Mitch Lasky's $13.5 million into Snapchat in 2013 and Peter Fenton's $10 million into Elasticsearch in 2012. The firm ran a London desk from 2000 and an Israeli desk from 2001; both became separate firms, Balderton Capital in 2007 and Benchmark Israel VC 2007 Ltd, and their books are excluded here. Benchmark held its funds at roughly $425 million for two decades, and broke that discipline in 2026: two vehicles raised in February to put about $225 million into a single Cerebras round, and $2 billion in June across a $750 million early-stage fund and Benchmark Partners T1, at $1.25 billion the firm's first dedicated growth fund. It reports as an exempt reporting adviser (CRD 160352) with 34 private funds carrying $7.58 billion of gross assets at the March-2026 ADV, and publishes no portfolio list at all — its website has been a single page with two addresses since 2013. The 284-company confirmed base runs from 1995 to 2026 and is overwhelmingly Series A entries, with 24 companies at $1 billion or more.
investment_concept: Benchmark backs founders at the first institutional round and takes a board seat, one equal partnership, one fund at a time.
